ns2:section.sectionText: Randomness has proven itself to be a useful resource for developing provably efficient algorithms and protocols. As a result, the study of randomized algorithms has become a major research topic in recent years. This course will explore techniques for effectively using randomization and for analyzing randomized algorithms, as well as examples from a variety of settings and problem areas. Topics covered would include basic probability, hashing, sampling, concentration inequalities (Chernoff), random processes (random walk, Markov chains, etc), learning, streaming, dimension reduction, and locality sensitive hashing. Algorithms for handling big data using these techniques would also be covered extensively.
ns2:section.sectionCappArea: Not intended for First Time Freshman students.
